title: Hot take: Gen AI is only good if you're willing to abandon your own creative direction
author: caliginous4
selftext:
Been trying to use chatgpt's image generation tools to build character, scene, and ship concept art for my game, and it just can't get it right. 

It can't stay consistent, despite OAI's claims. 

It can't reliably apply targeted feedback.

It can't take my own sketches and stay true to them in any regard.

The outputs kinda look ok if I had nothing in mind. 

The output sucks when I have something in mind.

I'm about to break down and use blender to design my own ships and other assets, but not being a strong blender user this is daunting. 

What do you do? What's your workflow for building something like a ship? 

Context for my game: 2d top down gameplay combined with manga style cutscene storyline images.

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body:
Go local and all kinds of new doors will open for you. :)

With various base models, LoRAs, inpainting and editing workflows, you will be free to create exactly what you want.

comments.author: angrylittledev
comments.body: Gen AI is more than just GPT, you being lazy and letting GPT use its default settings is on you, has nothing to do with Gen AI.

replies.author: caliginous4
replies.body: Fair enough. How do you harness gen ai better to be less lazy?

replies.author: angrylittledev
replies.body: Are you serious? Gen AI is just a blanket term, pick the tool you want and learn how to use it. There are local models that can be trained on your own art, you train your checkpoints and loras and then it will make exactly what you want, find the model that's most suitable for your current needs, then train it to suit your purposes. The more VRAM you have the better local tools you can use.

comments.author: RamonDozol
comments.body: I have been having much more sucess with Gemini.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: Gonna have to stop relying on generic ai generated art and come up with your own asset pipeline or use assets

replies.author: caliginous4
replies.body:
I mean yeah that's the point of this post.
I want to understand how others are using Gen AI in a way that's actually useful because my tests so far seem to conclude that I need to build my own assets

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body: Tbh you're going to have to do your own research or pay for that kind of information or tooling, you might get helpful tips here and there from asking around but theres not much of a reason for anyone to spend over an hour trying to explain something that might not even get used and will definitely not be credited. (speaking from past experience) So best of luck it won't be easy but at the same time its also never been easier

comments.author: Powerful-Storm-9092
comments.body: It probably just isn't possible to do it any better yet  we'll have to be patient. In the meantime, make everything else except the graphics perfect. The graphics will improve gradually as the AI ​​itself gets updated. That’s what I’m doing.

comments.author: __SlimeQ__
comments.body:
grok imagine's agent mode is great. you get like a canvas and you can organize all of the images you're generating and use them as input for new requests. and the agent can run python on the images too, so you can do basically any traditional image transform you can think of. there's no silver bullet in image generation though, you're still going to have complaints.

personally if i was building a ship i would say "hello claude opus 5 please use blender to build me a ship"

and if i really needed it to be 2d for some reason i'd say "and then make a sprite from it"

replies.author: caliginous4
replies.body: Awesome thanks, I'll check these out.
